trial_court: Family Court Judge, North District, Rohini Court, Delhi (MAT.APP.(F.C.) 372/2023)
facts_of_case: The respondent/wife filed a divorce petition under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The Family Court struck off the defence of the applicant/appellant/husband as litigation expenses had not been paid. The respondent/wife was accorded interim maintenance of Rs.5,000/- per month.

legal_principles.principle: The applicant/appellant/husband cannot be allowed to withdraw the appeal without complying with the order directing payment of interim maintenance.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the prayer made in the application, which is that the applicant/appellant/husband should be allowed to withdraw the appeal, with liberty to revive the same if and when the respondent's/ wife's divorce petition is restored cannot be accepted.

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot seek to have the best of both worlds by challenging orders while not complying with them.
legal_principles.held: The applicant/appellant/husband seeks the option to revive the appeal challenging orders that struck off his defence and ordered payment of interim maintenance while also not wanting to comply with the order that directed payment of interim maintenance.

outcome.result: Appeal allowed, subject to just exceptions
outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed with liberty to revive the same if and when the respondent's/ wife's divorce petition is restored.
